subproblems.title: Translation invariance of rectifiable varifolds (re-centring)
subproblems.statement: For all n, l in N, every set U in R^{n+l}, every contract rectifiable n-varifold V = v(M, theta) in U and every xi in R^{n+l}, there is a rectifiable n-varifold V' in U' := {x : x + xi in U} (the translate V - xi) such that: (0) the carrier of V' is M - xi, i.e. V'.carrier = (fun x => x - xi) '' V.carrier; (1) mu_{V'} is the image of mu_V under x |-> x - xi; (2) V'.mult x = theta(x + xi) for all x; (3) V'.tangentProj x = V.tangentProj (x + xi) for all x; (4) x in spt V' iff x + xi in spt V; (5) if V has generalized mean curvature H in U, then V' has generalized mean curvature H(. + xi) in U'; (6) V'.tiltExcess z s S = V.tiltExcess (z + xi) s S for all z, s, S; (7) V'.scaledLpNorm (H(. + xi)) p z s = V.scaledLpNorm H p (z + xi) s for all H, p, z, s.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (ξ : Amb n ℓ), ∃ V' : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ ((fun x => x + ξ) ⁻¹' U), V'.carrier = (fun x => x - ξ) '' V.carrier ∧ V'.weight = V.weight.map (fun x => x - ξ) ∧ (∀ x, V'.mult x = V.mult (x + ξ)) ∧ (∀ x, V'.tangentProj x = V.tangentProj (x + ξ)) ∧ (∀ x, x ∈ V'.support ↔ x + ξ ∈ V.support) ∧ (∀ H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ, V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H → V'.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature (fun x => H (x + ξ))) ∧ (∀ (z : Amb n ℓ) (s : ℝ) (S : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ)), V'.tiltExcess z s S = V.tiltExcess (z + ξ) s S) ∧ (∀ (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (p : ℝ) (z : Amb n ℓ) (s : ℝ), V'.scaledLpNorm (fun x => H (x + ξ)) p z s = V.scaledLpNorm H p (z + ξ) s)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation. tau(x) := x - xi, so tau^{-1}(y) = y + xi; U' := {x : x + xi in U} = tau(U). For the contract varifold V: M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, mu := V.weight = (H^n restricted to M).withDensity(ofReal o theta), p_x := V.tangentProj x, spt V := V.support = U cap spt mu. B_s(z) is the closed ball.

1. tau is an isometric bijection of R^{n+l}, hence a homeomorphism and a measurable equivalence. Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometries, so H^n(tau(A)) = H^n(A) for every A; consequently the image of H^n under tau is H^n, and for every A and every function g (nonnegative, or with values in a Banach space) int_{tau(A)} g dH^n = int_A g o tau dH^n. Because tau is a measurable equivalence, for every measure nu and every function g (integrable or not, Bochner or lower integral) int g d(tau_# nu) = int g o tau dnu and int_A g d(tau_# nu) = int_{tau^{-1}(A)} g o tau dnu (Mathlib MeasurableEquiv.integral_map, MeasurableEquiv.setIntegral_map / setLIntegral_map, lintegral_map_equiv).

2. Definition of V'. Carrier M' := tau(M) = (fun x => x - xi) '' M, the image of M under tau. Since tau is a bijection with inverse y |-> y + xi, also M' = {x : x + xi in M}. Multiplicity theta'(x) := theta(x + xi). Conclusion (0), V'.carrier = (fun x => x - xi) '' V.carrier, holds by this definition. The structure fields hold: (a) M' is contained in U' because M is contained in U. (b) M' is H^n-null-measurable: M = B cup N0 with B measurable and N0 contained in an H^n-null set; tau maps measurable sets to measurable sets and H^n-null sets to H^n-null sets (step 1). (c) M' is countably n-rectifiable: if M is contained in M_0 cup U_j F_j(R^n) with H^n(M_0) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz, then M' is contained in tau(M_0) cup U_j (tau o F_j)(R^n), H^n(tau(M_0)) = 0 and tau o F_j is Lipschitz with the same constant. (d) theta'(x) = theta(x + xi) > 0 for x in M'. (e) H^n restricted to M' is the image of H^n restricted to M under tau (step 1), and theta' = theta o tau^{-1}; composing an a.e.-measurable function with a measurable equivalence gives an a.e.-measurable function for the image measure, so theta' is AEMeasurable for H^n restricted to M'. (f) If K is compact and contained in U', then K + xi = tau^{-1}(K) is compact and contained in U, and int_{M' cap K} |theta'| dH^n = int_{M cap (K + xi)} |theta| dH^n < infinity by step 1, so theta' is integrable on M' cap K.

3. Conclusions (1) and (2). (2) is the definition of theta'. For a Borel set A, A cap M' = tau(tau^{-1}(A) cap M), so by step 1
mu'(A) = int_{A cap M'} ofReal theta'(x) dH^n(x) = int_{tau^{-1}(A) cap M} ofReal theta(y) dH^n(y) = mu(tau^{-1}(A)) = (tau_# mu)(A).
Two measures on the Borel sigma-algebra that agree on all Borel sets are equal, so mu' = tau_# mu, i.e. V'.weight = V.weight.map (fun x => x - xi).

4. Conclusion (3). Fix x. For every r > 0, blowUpMap x r '' M' = {r^{-1}(m - xi - x) : m in M} = blowUpMap (x + xi) r '' M, and theta'(x + r y) = theta((x + xi) + r y). Hence for every subspace P and every f in C_c(R^{n+l}) the functions of r appearing in Definition 1.7 (contract HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt) for (M', theta', x, P) and for (M, theta, x + xi, P) coincide, and so do the prescribed limits theta'(x) int_P f dH^n = theta(x + xi) int_P f dH^n; the dimension conditions are identical. Therefore the predicates P |-> HasWeighted(M', theta', x, P) and P |-> HasWeighted(M, theta, x + xi, P) are equal (funext/propext). V.tangentProj is defined by the expression `if h : exists P, pred P then (Classical.choose h).starProjection else 0`; applied to equal predicates it returns equal values in both branches. Thus p'_x = p_{x + xi} for every x.

5. Conclusion (4). For a homeomorphism tau, z has an open neighbourhood of (tau_# mu)-measure zero iff tau^{-1}(z) has an open neighbourhood of mu-measure zero; hence spt(tau_# mu) = tau(spt mu). Therefore spt V' = U' cap spt mu' = tau(U) cap tau(spt mu) = tau(U cap spt mu) = tau(spt V) (tau bijective), i.e. x in spt V' iff x + xi in spt V.

6. Conclusion (5). Suppose V has generalized mean curvature H in U and put H'(x) := H(x + xi).
(a) Local integrability. Let x in U'. Then x + xi in U, so there is a neighbourhood N of x + xi within U on which H is mu-integrable. tau(N) is a neighbourhood of x within U', and by step 1 int_{tau(N)} |H'| dmu' = int_N |H| dmu < infinity. Hence H' is locally integrable on U' with respect to mu'.
(b) First variation. Let X : R^{n+l} -> R^{n+l} be C^1 with compact support and tsupport X contained in U'. Put Y(y) := X(y - xi). Y is C^1 with compact support, tsupport Y = tsupport X + xi is contained in U, and DY(y) = DX(y - xi). By (3), div_{V'} X(x) = trace(DX(x) o p'_x) = trace(DY(x + xi) o p_{x + xi}) = div_V Y(x + xi) for every x, i.e. (div_{V'} X) o tau = div_V Y. By step 1 (change of variables for the image measure, valid for all functions), int div_{V'} X dmu' = int div_V Y dmu and int X . H' dmu' = int X(y - xi) . H(y) dmu(y) = int Y . H dmu. The first-variation identity of V applied to Y gives int div_{V'} X dmu' = - int X . H' dmu'.

7. Conclusion (6). By (3) and step 1, since tau^{-1}(B_s(z)) = B_s(z + xi):
int_{B_s(z)} |p'_x - p_S|^2 dmu'(x) = int_{B_s(z + xi)} |p_y - p_S|^2 dmu(y),
where |.|^2 is hsNormSq; multiplying by (s^n)^{-1} gives V'.tiltExcess z s S = V.tiltExcess (z + xi) s S.

8. Conclusion (7). In the same way, for every H, p, z, s: int^-_{B_s(z)} |H(x + xi)|^p dmu'(x) = int^-_{B_s(z + xi)} |H|^p dmu (lower integrals of nonnegative extended functions); multiplying by ofReal(s^{p-n}) and raising to the power 1/p gives V'.scaledLpNorm (fun x => H (x + xi)) p z s = V.scaledLpNorm H p (z + xi) s. This completes the proof.

Construct V' with carrier M' := tau(M) = (fun x => x - xi) '' M (conclusion (0)) and multiplicity theta(. + xi); verify all structure fields
mu_{V'} = tau_# mu_V on Borel sets
Blow-up sets and weights coincide, so the weighted tangent predicates are equal and tangentProj shifts
Support of an image measure under a homeomorphism: spt V' = spt V - xi
Local integrability and the first-variation identity transfer via Y = X(. - xi)
tiltExcess and scaledLpNorm shift by change of variables over balls

Cited results. [R1] Rademacher (Simon Ch. 2, 1.4; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableAt-type lemmas in Analysis/Calculus/Rademacher.lean): a map Lipschitz on an open set of R^n is differentiable L^n-a.e. there. [R2] Lebesgue differentiation for locally finite Borel measures on Euclidean space (Simon Ch. 1 Sect. 4; Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub): if lambda is locally finite and g in L^1_loc(lambda), then for lambda-a.e. x, lambda(B_r(x))^{-1} int_{B_r(x)} |g - g(x)| dlambda -> 0. [R3] Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2); SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6): if lambda is Borel regular and finite on compact subsets of an open set W and A is a lambda-measurable subset of W, then limsup_{r -> 0+} lambda(A cap B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x in W \ A. [R4] Area formula for injective Lipschitz maps (Simon Ch. 2 Sect. 3; SimonGMT Chapter02.injective_area_formula_lipschitz_simon, area_formula_lipschitzOn_multiplicity): if F is injective and Lipschitz on a Borel set Omega in R^n, then for Borel A in Omega and Borel g >= 0, int_{F(A)} g dH^n = int_A g(F(w)) J_F(w) dw, J_F(w) = det(DF(w)^* DF(w))^{1/2} at differentiability points; for an injective linear map the Jacobian is constant. [R5] Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 (using the C^1 approximation theorem, Ch. 2, 1.5): a countably n-rectifiable M satisfies M contained in N_0 cup U_{j>=1} N_j with H^n(N_0) = 0 and each N_j an embedded n-dimensional C^1 submanifold. [R6] SimonGMT HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique: if theta(x) != 0, HasWeighted(x, P) and HasWeighted(x, P') then P = P'. [R7] H^n is invariant under isometries, H^n(rA) = r^n H^n(A), H^n(F(A)) <= (Lip F)^n H^n(A) for Lipschitz F.

Proof.
1. Basic facts. (a) mu(A) = 0 whenever H^n(A cap M) = 0, and mu(R^{n+l} \ M) = 0. (b) mu(K) = int_{M cap K} theta dH^n < infinity for compact K contained in U (contract integrableOn_mult). (c) If x in M and HasWeighted(x, P), then the existential in the definition of tangentProj holds, its chosen witness equals P by [R6] (theta(x) > 0), and p_x = P.starProjection. (d) For x, r > 0, any set A and g nonnegative or integrable: int_{eta_{x,r}(A)} g dH^n = r^{-n} int_A g(eta_{x,r}(z)) dH^n(z) [R7].

2. Graph lemma. Fix q, f, R, L as in conclusion (4); assume R > 0 (otherwise (4) is vacuous). Put Omega := B°^n_R(0), F(w) := q(graphPoint(w, f(w))), Gamma := F(Omega), a := pi o q^{-1} with pi(graphPoint(w, y)) := w. For w in Omega at which f is differentiable put P_w := DF(w)(R^n) = span{q(graphPoint(v, Df(w) v)) : v in R^n}; DF(w) v = q(graphPoint(v, Df(w) v)) is injective, so finrank P_w = n.
Claim: there is an H^n-null set Z such that HasWeighted(x, P_{a(x)}) holds for every x in (M cap Gamma) \ Z (in particular f is differentiable at a(x)).
2.1. On the closed ball, |F(w) - F(w')|^2 = |w - w'|^2 + |f(w) - f(w')|^2 <= (1 + L^2)|w - w'|^2, F is injective and a o F = id with a 1-Lipschitz. Hence for A contained in Omega: L^n(A) <= H^n(F(A)) <= (1 + L^2)^{n/2} L^n(A) [R7]; F maps L^n-null sets to H^n-null sets; Gamma is sigma-compact (hence Borel) and H^n(Gamma) < infinity.
2.2. By [R1] f is differentiable at a.e. w in Omega, with ||Df(w)|| <= L there; let J_F(w) := det(I + Df(w)^T Df(w))^{1/2} in [1, (1 + L^2)^{n/2}] at such points and J_F := 1 elsewhere (bounded Borel). By [R2] for L^n, a.e. w in Omega is a Lebesgue point of J_F. Let Z_1 be the L^n-null set of w in Omega where f is not differentiable or which are not Lebesgue points of J_F; H^n(F(Z_1)) = 0 by 2.1. By [R4], int_{F(A)} g dH^n = int_A g(F(w)) J_F(w) dw for Borel A in Omega and Borel g >= 0.
2.3. Tangent plane of Gamma. Let w in Omega \ Z_1, x := F(w), P := P_w, and g in C_c(R^{n+l}) with spt g in B_K(0), |g| <= G. With Phi_r(z) := (F(w + r z) - F(w))/r, by 1(d) and 2.2,
int_{eta_{x,r}(Gamma)} g dH^n = r^{-n} int_Omega g((F(w') - F(w))/r) J_F(w') dw' = int_{(Omega - w)/r} g(Phi_r(z)) J_F(w + r z) dz.
Since |Phi_r(z)| >= |z| the integrand vanishes for |z| > K, and B_K(0) is contained in (Omega - w)/r for small r. Differentiability gives Phi_r(z) -> DF(w) z for every z, so int_{B_K} g(Phi_r(z)) J_F(w) dz -> int_{R^n} g(DF(w) z) J_F(w) dz by dominated convergence, while |int_{B_K} g(Phi_r(z)) (J_F(w + r z) - J_F(w)) dz| <= G r^{-n} int_{B_{rK}(w)} |J_F - J_F(w)| -> 0 (Lebesgue point). By [R4] for the injective linear map DF(w), int_{R^n} g(DF(w) z) J_F(w) dz = int_P g dH^n. Hence lim_{r -> 0+} int_{eta_{x,r}(Gamma)} g dH^n = int_P g dH^n for all g in C_c. Testing with 0 <= g <= 1 equal to 1 on B_1(0) and supported in B_{1+e}(0), resp. equal to 1 on B_{1-e}(0) and supported in B_1(0), and letting e -> 0, also H^n(Gamma cap B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> 1.
2.4. Densities of the complements. (a) [R3] with W := U, lambda := mu (finite on compacts of U by 1(b)), A := M \ Gamma (mu-measurable): for H^n-a.e. x in U \ (M \ Gamma), in particular H^n-a.e. x in M cap Gamma, r^{-n} int_{(M \ Gamma) cap B_r(x)} theta dH^n = r^{-n} mu((M \ Gamma) cap B_r(x)) -> 0. (b) [R3] with W := R^{n+l}, lambda := H^n restricted to Gamma (finite by 2.1), A := Gamma \ M: for H^n-a.e. x in M, r^{-n} H^n((Gamma \ M) cap B_r(x)) -> 0.
2.5. Lebesgue points of theta. lambda_3 := H^n restricted to M cap Gamma is a finite Borel measure. For each compact K contained in U, theta 1_K is lambda_3-integrable, so by [R2] for lambda_3-a.e. x in the interior of K the averages lambda_3(B_r(x))^{-1} int_{B_r(x)} |theta - theta(x)| dlambda_3 tend to 0 (for small r, B_r(x) is contained in K); exhausting U by countably many such K, this holds for lambda_3-a.e. x in U. At points x in M cap Gamma where 2.3 and 2.4(b) also hold, lambda_3(B_r(x)) <= H^n(Gamma cap B_r(x)) <= 2 omega_n r^n for small r, hence r^{-n} int_{M cap Gamma cap B_r(x)} |theta - theta(x)| dH^n -> 0.
2.6. Let Z be the union of F(Z_1) and the H^n-null exceptional sets of 2.4(a), 2.4(b) and 2.5 (H^n-null because lambda_3-null subsets of M cap Gamma are H^n-null). Let x in (M cap Gamma) \ Z, w := a(x) (so x = F(w), w in Omega \ Z_1), P := P_w, g in C_c with spt g in B_K(0) and |g| <= G, and r so small that B_{Kr}(x) is contained in U. By 1(d),
int_{eta_{x,r}(M)} g(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y) = r^{-n} int_M g(eta_{x,r} z) theta(z) dH^n(z)
= theta(x) r^{-n} int_Gamma g(eta_{x,r} z) dH^n - theta(x) r^{-n} int_{Gamma \ M} g(eta_{x,r} z) dH^n + r^{-n} int_{M cap Gamma} g(eta_{x,r} z)(theta(z) - theta(x)) dH^n + r^{-n} int_{M \ Gamma} g(eta_{x,r} z) theta(z) dH^n.
By 2.3 and 1(d) the first term tends to theta(x) int_P g dH^n; the second is at most theta(x) G r^{-n} H^n((Gamma \ M) cap B_{Kr}(x)) -> 0 by 2.4(b); the third is at most G r^{-n} int_{M cap Gamma cap B_{Kr}(x)} |theta - theta(x)| dH^n -> 0 by 2.5; the fourth is at most G r^{-n} int_{(M \ Gamma) cap B_{Kr}(x)} theta dH^n -> 0 by 2.4(a). Thus HasWeighted(x, P_w), proving the claim.

3. Conclusion (4). With Z from step 2, mu(Z) = 0 by 1(a), and mu(Gamma \ M) = 0. Let x be outside Z cup (Gamma \ M) and suppose x = q(graphPoint(x', f(x'))) with x' in B°^n_R(0) and f differentiable at x'. Then x in M cap Gamma \ Z and a(x) = x', so HasWeighted(x, P_{x'}); by 1(c), p_x = P_{x'}.starProjection with P_{x'} = span(range(v |-> q(graphPoint(v, fderiv f x' v)))). Hence (4) holds for mu-a.e. x.

4. Countable C^1-graph cover of M. By [R5], M is contained in N_0 cup U_j N_j. Let y in N_j and choose a linear isometry q_y with q_y(R^n x {0}) = T_y N_j. By the implicit function theorem there are c in R^n, s > 0, a C^1 map g defined on a neighbourhood of the closed ball B^n_s(c), and an open set W_y containing y such that N_j cap W_y = q_y({graphPoint(w, g(w)) : w in B°^n_s(c)}). By second countability countably many W_y cover N_j. g is Lipschitz on the convex compact set B^n_s(c); extend it componentwise (McShane; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real) to a Lipschitz map f : R^n -> R^l and choose R > |c| + s. We obtain countably many (q_k, f_k, R_k) and open balls B_k := B°^n_{s_k}(c_k) contained in B°^n_{R_k}(0), with f_k Lipschitz on R^n and f_k = g_k on the closed ball (so f_k is C^1 on the open ball B_k, with Df_k = Dg_k continuous there; nothing is claimed outside B_k), such that, with F_k(w) := q_k(graphPoint(w, f_k(w))) and G_k := F_k(B_k), M is contained in N_0 cup U_k G_k.

5. Conclusions (0) and (1). Apply step 2 to each (q_k, f_k, R_k) and obtain H^n-null sets Z^k. E := N_0 cup U_k Z^k is H^n-null, so mu(E) = 0. Each x in M \ E lies in some G_k, contained in F_k(B°^n_{R_k}(0)), so HasWeighted(x, P^k_{a_k(x)}): this is (0). For such x, theta(x) > 0, so by 1(c) p_x = (P^k_{a_k(x)}).starProjection with finrank n: this is (1). Since mu(R^{n+l} \ M) = 0, both hold mu-a.e.

6. Conclusion (2). For each k, Pi_k(x) := orthogonal projection onto DF_k(a_k(x))(R^n) is continuous on G_k: a_k is continuous, w |-> Df_k(w) = Dg_k(w) is continuous on the open ball B_k, and the orthogonal projection onto the range of the injective linear map A_w := DF_k(w) is A_w (A_w^* A_w)^{-1} A_w^*, continuous in w. G_k is Borel (the continuous injective image of a sigma-compact set is sigma-compact). Define Pi(x) := Pi_k(x) for x in G_k \ U_{i<k} G_i and Pi(x) := 0 off U_k G_k. Pi is Borel measurable into the finite-dimensional normed space of linear maps, and for x in M \ E, if x in G_k \ U_{i<k} G_i then x is not in Z^k, so p_x = Pi_k(x) = Pi(x) by step 5. Hence p = Pi mu-a.e., and x |-> p_x is AEStronglyMeasurable for mu.

7. Conclusion (3). Let x in M with HasWeighted(x, P) (mu-a.e. x by (0)). For e in (0,1) choose g_1, g_2 in C_c(R^{n+l}; [0,1]) with g_1 = 1 on B_{1-e}(0), spt g_1 in B_1(0), g_2 = 1 on B_1(0), spt g_2 in B_{1+e}(0). By 1(d), for r > 0 with B_{2r}(x) contained in U:
int_{eta_{x,r}(M)} g_1(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y) <= r^{-n} int_{M cap B_r(x)} theta dH^n = r^{-n} mu(B_r(x)) <= int_{eta_{x,r}(M)} g_2(y) theta(x + r y) dH^n(y).
Letting r -> 0+ and then e -> 0, and using omega_n (1 - e)^n <= int_P g_1 dH^n <= int_P g_2 dH^n <= omega_n (1 + e)^n, we get mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> theta(x). As omega_n r^n is in (0, infinity), this is V.HasDensity x (theta x) (quotient in [0, infinity], limit ofReal theta(x)). Hence (3) holds mu-a.e.
proof_key_steps: mu is absolutely continuous w.r.t. H^n on M; uniqueness of weighted tangents identifies tangentProj with any weighted tangent plane on M
Graph lemma: area formula, Rademacher and Lebesgue points give the unweighted tangent plane of a Lipschitz graph
Upper density theorem for M \ Gamma and Gamma \ M, and Lebesgue points of theta
Weighted tangent plane of M equals the graph tangent plane H^n-a.e. on M cap Gamma: conclusion (4)
Cover M up to an H^n-null set by countably many C^1 graphs (Ch. 3 Lemma 1.2, implicit function theorem, McShane)
Existence and rank-n projection a.e.; a Borel representative gives measurability
Density equals multiplicity from the weighted blow-up limit

subproblems.title: Monotonicity inequality with L^p mean curvature for contract varifolds (Simon Ch. 4, 4.1-4.8)
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0, p > n, U open in R^{n+l}, and V a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U with generalized mean curvature H in U; mu := V.weight, kappa := (p-n)/(4p), alpha := 1 - n/p. Let y in R^{n+l}, 0 < R < S and Lambda > 0 with B_S(y) contained in U, integral_{B_S(y)} |H|^p dmu < infinity (lower integral) and (R^{p-n} integral_{B_R(y)} |H|^p dmu)^{1/p} <= kappa Lambda (V.scaledLpNorm H p y R <= ofReal(kappa Lambda)). Then there is F : R -> R such that (i) for 0 < r <= R: e^{-Lambda} <= F(r) <= e^Lambda, |F(r) - 1| <= (1/2) e^{Lambda/2} Lambda (r/R)^alpha, and |F(r) - 1| <= Lambda (r/R)^alpha if Lambda <= 1; (ii) Phi(t) := F(t) t^{-n} mu(B_t(y)) + F(t) - 1 is nondecreasing on (0, R]: Phi(s) <= Phi(r) whenever 0 < s <= r <= R (closed balls B_t(y); mu(B_t(y)) < infinity is used as a real number).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ), V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H → ∀ (y : Amb n ℓ) (R S Λ : ℝ), 0 < R → R < S → 0 < Λ → closedBall y S ⊆ U → ∫⁻ x in closedBall y S, ‖H x‖ₑ ^ p ∂V.weight < ⊤ → V.scaledLpNorm H p y R ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((p - n) / (4 * p) * Λ) → ∃ F : ℝ → ℝ, (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r ≤ R → Real.exp (-Λ) ≤ F r ∧ F r ≤ Real.exp Λ ∧ |F r - 1| ≤ Real.exp (Λ / 2) / 2 * Λ * (r / R) ^ (1 - (n : ℝ) / p) ∧ (Λ ≤ 1 → |F r - 1| ≤ Λ * (r / R) ^ (1 - (n : ℝ) / p))) ∧ ∀ s r : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ r → r ≤ R → F s * ((V.weight (closedBall y s)).toReal / s ^ n) + (F s - 1) ≤ F r * ((V.weight (closedBall y r)).toReal / r ^ n) + (F r - 1)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 4, 3.2-3.5 and 4.1-4.8 (radial first variation with the epsilon-cutoff, Hoelder bound, integrating factor, epsilon -> 0). The coefficient in front of Lambda in 4.2 is taken to be kappa = (p-n)/(4p), the value for which the integration after 4.4 yields the bounds 4.5-4.6; this constant agrees with lpMeanCurvatureKappa of the SimonGMT Chapter04 files, but no Chapter04 result is used. Only the monotonicity consequence 4.8 is proved, i.e. the inequality Phi(s) <= Phi(r); for it only the sign of the J-term of 3.4 is needed. This argument is carried out directly for the contract varifold and uses no Chapter04 library structure.

Notation. mu := V.weight; p_x := V.tangentProj x; B_t(y) := closedBall y t (closed ball); r(x) := |x - y| and nu(x) := (x - y)/r(x) for x != y. kappa := (p - n)/(4p) > 0 and alpha := 1 - n/p in (0,1), so kappa/alpha = 1/4. For 0 < t <= S put ||H||_t := (integral^-_{B_t(y)} |H|^p dmu)^{1/p}, where integral^- is the lower (lintegral) integral of the extended function |H|^p. This is finite because t <= S and the hypothesis bounds the integral over B_S(y), and it is nondecreasing in t. K(y,R) := V.scaledLpNorm H p y R = (ofReal(R^{p-n}) integral^-_{B_R(y)} |H|^p dmu)^{1/p} = R^alpha ||H||_R, since ofReal(R^{p-n})^{1/p} = ofReal(R^alpha). The hypothesis K(y,R) <= ofReal(kappa Lambda) therefore gives ||H||_R <= kappa Lambda R^{-alpha}.

0. Preliminaries.
(a) By ted_tangent_plane_facts, conclusions (1) and (2) (applicable since n >= 1 and U is open): for mu-a.e. x, p_x = P.starProjection for an n-dimensional subspace P. Hence p_x is self-adjoint and idempotent, trace p_x = n and |p_x v| <= |v|. Moreover x |-> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable.
(b) B_S(y) is a compact subset of U, so mu(B_S(y)) < infinity (V.integrableOn_mult). H is mu-integrable on B_S(y): the first conjunct of V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H makes H locally integrable on U, hence integrable on compact subsets of U.
(c) Hoelder. Let g be mu-measurable with 0 <= g <= 1 and g = 0 outside B_t(y) for some t <= S. Then integral g |H| dmu <= ||H||_t (integral g dmu)^{1-1/p}. This is Hoelder with exponents p and p/(p-1) (note p > n >= 1, so p > 1), using g^{p/(p-1)} <= g.
(d) Elementary: a^{1-1/p} <= 1 + a for a >= 0, and |e^u - 1| <= |u| e^{|u|} for real u.

1. Cutoffs. Let chi(t) := 1 for t <= 0, chi(t) := 1 - 3t^2 + 2t^3 for 0 <= t <= 1, and chi(t) := 0 for t >= 1. chi is C^1 and nonincreasing with 0 <= chi <= 1; chi'(t) = -6t(1-t) on [0,1], chi' = 0 outside (0,1), and |chi'| <= 3/2.
For eps in (0,1] let phi_eps(t) := chi((t - 1)/eps). Then phi_eps is C^1 and nonincreasing, 0 <= phi_eps <= 1, phi_eps = 1 on (-infinity,1], phi_eps = 0 on [1+eps, infinity), phi_eps' <= 0, phi_eps' = 0 on (-infinity,1], and |phi_eps'| <= 3/(2 eps). For each t, phi_eps(t) tends to the indicator of (-infinity,1] at t as eps -> 0+ (if t > 1, phi_eps(t) = 0 as soon as eps < t - 1).

2. Radial first variation (Simon 3.2-3.4, 4.1). Fix eps in (0,1] and put T_eps := S/(1 + eps). For rho in (0, T_eps) let X_rho(x) := phi_eps(r(x)/rho)(x - y).
(a) X_rho is C^1. On the open set {r < rho} it equals x - y, because phi_eps = 1 on (-infinity,1]. On the open set {x != y} it is built from C^1 maps by composition and products. X_rho vanishes outside B_{(1+eps) rho}(y), so it has compact support and tsupport X_rho ⊆ B_{(1+eps) rho}(y) ⊆ B_S(y) ⊆ U (as (1+eps) rho < S). Hence X_rho is an admissible field in V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H.
(b) For x != y, D X_rho(x) v = phi_eps(r/rho) v + rho^{-1} phi_eps'(r/rho) (nu . v)(x - y), and D X_rho(x) = I where r < rho. Let x be a point where p_x is a rank-n orthogonal projection (mu-a.e. x, by 0(a)). The map v |-> (nu . p_x v) w has trace (p_x nu) . w, and (p_x nu) . (x - y) = r |p_x nu|^2. Hence
 div_M X_rho(x) = trace(D X_rho(x) o p_x) = n phi_eps(r/rho) + (r/rho) phi_eps'(r/rho) |p_x nu|^2.
The second term is 0 where r <= rho, in particular at x = y. Since phi_eps' <= 0 and 0 <= |p_x nu|^2 <= 1,
 div_M X_rho(x) >= n phi_eps(r/rho) + (r/rho) phi_eps'(r/rho) for mu-a.e. x. (2.1)
(c) Integrability. div_M X_rho is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, by 0(a) and continuity of D X_rho. It is bounded by n + (1+eps) 3/(2 eps) and vanishes outside B_S(y). Also X_rho . H is integrable, since |X_rho| <= S and H is integrable on B_S(y). The first-variation identity gives
 integral div_M X_rho dmu = - L(rho), where L(rho) := integral phi_eps(r/rho)(x - y) . H dmu.
(d) Let I(rho) := integral phi_eps(r/rho) dmu. For fixed x, rho |-> phi_eps(r(x)/rho) is C^1 on (0, infinity) with derivative -(r/rho^2) phi_eps'(r/rho). This derivative vanishes unless rho <= r <= (1+eps) rho, and is then bounded by (1+eps) rho^{-1} 3/(2 eps). For rho in a compact interval [a, b] of (0, T_eps) the derivatives are therefore bounded by 3/(a eps) and vanish outside B_S(y), which has finite measure. Differentiation under the integral sign shows that I is differentiable on (0, T_eps) with I'(rho) = - integral (r/rho^2) phi_eps'(r/rho) dmu, so integral (r/rho) phi_eps'(r/rho) dmu = - rho I'(rho). L is continuous on (0, T_eps) by dominated convergence: the integrand is continuous in rho and dominated by S |H| on B_S(y).
(e) Integrating (2.1) and using (c) and (d) gives -L(rho) >= n I(rho) - rho I'(rho). Hence, for rho in (0, T_eps),
 d/drho (rho^{-n} I(rho)) = rho^{-n-1}(rho I'(rho) - n I(rho)) >= rho^{-n-1} L(rho). (2.2)

3. Hoelder bound (Simon 4.2-4.3). Since phi_eps(r/rho) = 0 for r >= (1+eps) rho, we have |(x - y) . H| phi_eps(r/rho) <= (1+eps) rho |H| phi_eps(r/rho). By 0(c) with g = phi_eps(r/rho) and t = (1+eps) rho,
 |L(rho)| <= (1+eps) rho ||H||_{(1+eps) rho} I(rho)^{1-1/p}.
Hence, by 0(d),
 |rho^{-n-1} L(rho)| <= (1+eps) ||H||_{(1+eps) rho} rho^{-n/p} (rho^{-n} I(rho))^{1-1/p} <= (1+eps) ||H||_{(1+eps) rho} rho^{-n/p} (1 + rho^{-n} I(rho)).
Define a_eps(rho) := rho^{-n-1} L(rho)/(1 + rho^{-n} I(rho)) for rho in (0, T_eps). It is continuous and satisfies
 |a_eps(rho)| <= (1+eps) ||H||_{(1+eps) rho} rho^{-n/p} <= 2 ||H||_S rho^{-n/p}. (3.1)
Since n/p < 1, rho^{-n/p} is integrable on (0, b] for every b > 0.

4. Integrating factor (Simon 4.4). For rho in (0, T_eps) put F_eps(rho) := exp(- integral_0^rho a_eps(t) dt), which is finite by (3.1), and Psi_eps(rho) := F_eps(rho)(1 + rho^{-n} I(rho)). By the fundamental theorem of calculus (a_eps is continuous), F_eps is differentiable with F_eps' = - a_eps F_eps. By (2.2),
 Psi_eps'(rho) = F_eps(rho) [d/drho(rho^{-n} I(rho)) - a_eps(rho)(1 + rho^{-n} I(rho))] = F_eps(rho) [d/drho(rho^{-n} I(rho)) - rho^{-n-1} L(rho)] >= 0.
By the mean value theorem, Psi_eps is nondecreasing on (0, T_eps). (4.1)

5. Letting eps -> 0 (Simon 3.5-3.6, 4.5-4.7). Choose eps_1 in (0,1] with (1 + eps_1) R < S and put eps_k := eps_1/k. Then R < T_{eps_k} for every k. Write I_k, L_k, a_k, F_k, Psi_k for the objects of Steps 2-4 with eps = eps_k; all are defined on (0, R].
(a) Let t in (0, R]. Then I_k(t) -> mu(B_t(y)) and L_k(t) -> L_0(t) := integral_{B_t(y)} (x - y) . H dmu, by dominated convergence. Indeed phi_{eps_k}(r/t) -> indicator{r <= t} pointwise, and the integrands vanish outside B_{(1+eps_1) R}(y) ⊆ B_S(y), where they are dominated by 1 and S |H| respectively. Hence a_k(t) -> a_0(t) := t^{-n-1} L_0(t)/(1 + t^{-n} mu(B_t(y))). As a pointwise limit of continuous functions, a_0 is measurable on (0, R].
(b) By 0(c) with g the indicator of B_t(y), |L_0(t)| <= t ||H||_t mu(B_t(y))^{1-1/p}. As in Step 3, for 0 < t <= R,
 |a_0(t)| <= ||H||_t t^{-n/p} <= ||H||_R t^{-n/p} <= kappa Lambda R^{-1} (t/R)^{-n/p},
using ||H||_R <= kappa Lambda R^{-alpha} = kappa Lambda R^{-1} R^{n/p}. Integrating, with kappa/alpha = 1/4:
 integral_0^rho |a_0(t)| dt <= kappa Lambda R^{-1} integral_0^rho (t/R)^{-n/p} dt = (kappa/alpha) Lambda (rho/R)^alpha = (Lambda/4)(rho/R)^alpha, 0 < rho <= R. (5.1)
(c) By (3.1), |a_k(t)| <= 2 ||H||_S t^{-n/p} on (0, R]. By dominated convergence, integral_0^rho a_k -> integral_0^rho a_0 for each rho in (0, R]. Define F(rho) := exp(- integral_0^rho a_0(t) dt) for 0 < rho <= R, and F(rho) := 1 for all other real rho. Then F_k(rho) -> F(rho) for rho in (0, R].
(d) Conclusion (i). Let 0 < r <= R and b := (Lambda/4)(r/R)^alpha, so b is in (0, Lambda/4]. By (5.1), |log F(r)| <= b, so e^{-Lambda} <= e^{-b} <= F(r) <= e^b <= e^Lambda. By 0(d),
 |F(r) - 1| <= b e^b <= (1/4) e^{Lambda/4} Lambda (r/R)^alpha <= (1/2) e^{Lambda/2} Lambda (r/R)^alpha.
If Lambda <= 1, then b e^b <= (e^{1/4}/4) Lambda (r/R)^alpha <= Lambda (r/R)^alpha.
(e) Conclusion (ii). Let 0 < s <= r <= R. By (4.1), Psi_k(s) <= Psi_k(r) for every k, and by (a) and (c), Psi_k(t) -> F(t)(1 + t^{-n} mu(B_t(y))) for t in {s, r}. Hence F(s)(1 + s^{-n} mu(B_s(y))) <= F(r)(1 + r^{-n} mu(B_r(y))). This is Phi(s) <= Phi(r) with Phi(t) = F(t) t^{-n} mu(B_t(y)) + F(t) - 1. Since mu(B_t(y)) <= mu(B_S(y)) < infinity, the number t^{-n} mu(B_t(y)) is (V.weight (closedBall y t)).toReal / t^n, as in the statement.
proof_key_steps: ted_tangent_plane_facts (1),(2): p_x is mu-a.e. a rank-n orthogonal projection and mu-measurable; H is integrable and mu finite on B_S(y)
First variation with X = phi_eps(|x-y|/rho)(x-y): since phi_eps' <= 0 and |p_x nu| <= 1, d/drho(rho^-n I) >= rho^(-n-1) L
Hoelder: |rho^(-n-1) L| <= (1+eps)||H||_{(1+eps)rho} rho^(-n/p)(1 + rho^-n I); a_eps := rho^(-n-1) L/(1 + rho^-n I)
Integrating factor F_eps = exp(-int_0^rho a_eps) makes F_eps(1 + rho^-n I) nondecreasing
eps -> 0 along eps_k: I_k -> mu(B_t), L_k -> L_0, a_k -> a_0 (dominated by 2||H||_S t^(-n/p)); F := exp(-int_0^rho a_0) with int|a_0| <= (Lambda/4)(rho/R)^alpha since kappa/alpha = 1/4
Bounds (i) from |log F(r)| <= (Lambda/4)(r/R)^alpha; monotonicity (ii) is the limit of the monotonicity of F_eps(1 + rho^-n I)

subproblems.title: Density at least one on the support inside B_rho(0) under the Allard hypotheses (Simon Ch. 4, 4.9-4.10)
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0, p > n, U open in R^{n+l}, V a contract rectifiable n-varifold in U, H : R^{n+l} -> R^{n+l}, and delta, rho real numbers with AllardHypotheses H p delta rho (rho > 0, V has generalized mean curvature H in U, theta >= 1 mu-a.e., 0 in spt V, B_rho(0) contained in U, mu(B_rho(0)) <= (1+delta) omega_n rho^n, (rho^{p-n} integral_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p dmu)^{1/p} <= delta). Then for every y in spt V with |y| < rho and every eps > 0 there is s_0 > 0 such that mu(B_s(y)) >= (1 - eps) omega_n s^n for all s in (0, s_0) (stated as the eventual inequality ofReal((1 - eps) omega_n s^n) <= mu(B_s(y)) along s -> 0+; B_s(y) closed, omega_n = unitBallVolume n).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ : ℝ), V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → ∀ y ∈ V.support ∩ ball (0 : Amb n ℓ) ρ, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ENNReal.ofReal ((1 - ε) * (unitBallVolume n * s ^ n)) ≤ V.weight (closedBall y s)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 4, 3.9-3.13 (existence and upper semicontinuity of the density from the monotonicity formula), 4.9 and Remark 4.10(1) (the L^p case with theta >= 1), with Theta = theta mu-a.e. from Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2). Here these inputs are ted_lp_monotonicity and ted_tangent_plane_facts (3).

Notation. mu := V.weight; theta := V.mult; spt V := V.support = U cap spt mu. B_s(z) := closedBall z s is the closed ball and B°_s(z) := ball z s the open ball. omega_n := unitBallVolume n > 0 and K(z,s) := V.scaledLpNorm H p z s. kappa := (p - n)/(4p) > 0 and alpha := 1 - n/p in (0,1).
(F2) mu(K) < infinity for every compact K ⊆ U (V.integrableOn_mult).
(K-mono) If 0 < s <= t and B_s(z) ⊆ B_t(w), then K(z,s) <= K(w,t). Indeed s^{p-n} <= t^{p-n} as p > n, the lower integral of |H|^p over B_s(z) is at most that over B_t(w), and a |-> a^{1/p} is monotone on [0, infinity].
(A) AllardHypotheses H p delta rho states: rho > 0; V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H; theta >= 1 mu-a.e.; 0 in spt V; B_rho(0) ⊆ U; mu(B_rho(0)) <= ofReal((1+delta) omega_n rho^n); and K(0,rho) <= ofReal(delta). Since ofReal(rho^{p-n}) > 0 and K(0,rho) < infinity, integral^-_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p dmu < infinity. By (K-mono), K(z,s) <= ofReal(delta) whenever 0 < s <= rho and B_s(z) ⊆ B_rho(0).

1. Uniform hypotheses on W := B°_rho(0). Put Lambda := max(delta, 0)/kappa + 1 > 0. Then kappa Lambda = max(delta, 0) + kappa >= max(delta, 0), so ofReal(delta) <= ofReal(kappa Lambda). For z in W let d(z) := rho - |z| > 0, R_z := d(z)/4 and S_z := d(z)/2. Then:
- 0 < R_z < S_z, and B_{S_z}(z) ⊆ B°_rho(0) ⊆ B_rho(0) ⊆ U, since |x| <= |z| + d(z)/2 < rho;
- integral^-_{B_{S_z}(z)} |H|^p dmu <= integral^-_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p dmu < infinity;
- K(z, R_z) <= ofReal(delta) <= ofReal(kappa Lambda), by (A) and R_z <= rho.

2. Existence of the density on W (Simon 3.9, 4.9). Fix z in W. By Step 1 and V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H from (A), ted_lp_monotonicity applies at (y, R, S, Lambda) := (z, R_z, S_z, Lambda). It gives F_z with e^{-Lambda} <= F_z(t) <= e^Lambda and |F_z(t) - 1| <= c(t/R_z) for t in (0, R_z], where c(u) := (1/2) e^{Lambda/2} Lambda u^alpha. The function c is increasing on [0, infinity) and c(u) -> 0 as u -> 0+. It also gives that Phi_z(t) := F_z(t) t^{-n} mu(B_t(z)) + F_z(t) - 1 is nondecreasing on (0, R_z].
Since Phi_z(t) >= F_z(t) - 1 >= e^{-Lambda} - 1, the limit l_z := lim_{t -> 0+} Phi_z(t) = inf_{(0, R_z]} Phi_z exists in R, and l_z <= Phi_z(t) for t in (0, R_z]. As F_z(t) -> 1, t^{-n} mu(B_t(z)) = (Phi_z(t) - F_z(t) + 1)/F_z(t) -> l_z. Put Theta(z) := l_z/omega_n. Thus mu(B_t(z))/(omega_n t^n) -> Theta(z) as t -> 0+, and Theta(z) >= 0.

3. Upper semicontinuity of Theta on W (Simon 3.11, 4.9). Fix z in W and put r_1 := d(z)/8. Let |z' - z| <= r_1. Then z' in W, d(z') >= 7 d(z)/8, and R_{z'} >= 7 d(z)/32 > r_1. For 0 < t <= r_1, Step 2 for z' gives F_{z'}(t) - 1 <= c(t/R_{z'}) <= c(t/r_1), and hence
 omega_n Theta(z') = l_{z'} <= Phi_{z'}(t) <= (1 + c(t/r_1)) t^{-n} mu(B_t(z')) + c(t/r_1).
If moreover |z' - z| <= eta with 0 < eta <= r_1, then B_t(z') ⊆ B_{t+eta}(z), so
 omega_n Theta(z') <= (1 + c(t/r_1)) t^{-n} mu(B_{t+eta}(z)) + c(t/r_1).
Hence limsup_{z' -> z} omega_n Theta(z') <= (1 + c(t/r_1)) t^{-n} mu(B_{t+eta}(z)) + c(t/r_1) for all such eta and t. Now let eta -> 0+: the closed balls B_{t+eta}(z) decrease to B_t(z) and have finite measure, so mu(B_{t+eta}(z)) -> mu(B_t(z)). Then let t -> 0+: c(t/r_1) -> 0 and t^{-n} mu(B_t(z)) -> omega_n Theta(z). Therefore limsup_{z' -> z} Theta(z') <= Theta(z).

4. Theta = theta >= 1 mu-a.e. on W (Simon 3.12; Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)). By ted_tangent_plane_facts (3), for mu-a.e. x, V.HasDensity x (theta x) holds: mu(B_t(x))/ofReal(omega_n t^n) -> ofReal(theta(x)) in [0, infinity] as t -> 0+. By (A), theta(x) >= 1 for mu-a.e. x. Let x in W be a point where both hold. For t in (0, R_x], mu(B_t(x)) is finite and omega_n t^n > 0, so the quotient equals ofReal(mu(B_t(x)).toReal/(omega_n t^n)). This tends to ofReal(Theta(x)) by Step 2 and continuity of ofReal. By uniqueness of limits, ofReal(Theta(x)) = ofReal(theta(x)). Since theta(x) >= 1 > 0 and Theta(x) >= 0, Theta(x) = theta(x) >= 1. Hence {x in W : Theta(x) < 1} is contained in a mu-null set.

5. Conclusion (Simon 4.10(1)). The set O := {x in W : Theta(x) < 1} is open: if x in O, then by Step 3, limsup_{z' -> x} Theta(z') <= Theta(x) < 1, so Theta < 1 on a neighbourhood of x contained in W. By Step 4, mu(O) = 0. A point of spt mu has no open neighbourhood of mu-measure 0, so O cap spt mu is empty.
Now let y in spt V cap B°_rho(0). Then y in spt mu cap W, hence Theta(y) >= 1. Let eps > 0. Since mu(B_s(y))/(omega_n s^n) -> Theta(y) >= 1 > 1 - eps, there is s_0 > 0 with mu(B_s(y)).toReal >= (1 - eps) omega_n s^n for all s in (0, s_0). As mu(B_s(y)) < infinity, this gives ofReal((1 - eps)(omega_n s^n)) <= mu(B_s(y)); if (1 - eps) omega_n s^n <= 0 the left side is 0 anyway. This is the asserted eventual inequality along s -> 0+ (the filter 𝓝[>] 0).
proof_key_steps: Uniform hypotheses on W = B°_rho(0) with Lambda = max(delta,0)/kappa + 1; for z in W the ball B_{d/2}(z), d = rho - |z|, lies in B°_rho(0)
ted_lp_monotonicity at z with R = d/4, S = d/2: Phi_z is nondecreasing and F_z -> 1, so Theta(z) = lim mu(B_t(z))/(omega_n t^n) exists
Upper semicontinuity of Theta on W from the uniform bound |F - 1| <= c(t/r_1) and B_t(z') ⊆ B_{t+eta}(z)
Theta = theta >= 1 mu-a.e. on W from ted_tangent_plane_facts (3) and theta >= 1 a.e.
{Theta < 1} ∩ W is open and mu-null, hence misses spt mu; Theta(y) >= 1 gives the eventual lower bound

subproblems.title: Mass, multiplicity and carrier bounds under the Allard hypotheses (Simon 2.4)
subproblems.statement: For n >= 1, l and p > n there are C >= 1 and delta_P in (0, 1/8] with C delta_P <= 1/2 (depending only on n, l, p) such that, whenever U is open, V has generalized mean curvature H in U and AllardHypotheses H p delta rho hold with 0 < delta <= delta_P: (i) mu(B_s(y)) <= (1 + C delta) omega_n s^n for all y with |y| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < s <= rho/2; (ii) mu(B_s(y)) >= (1 - C delta) omega_n s^n if moreover y in spt V; (iii) theta(x) <= 1 + C delta for mu-a.e. x with |x| <= 3 delta rho; (iv) H^n((spt V cap B°_rho(0)) \ M) = 0. (mu = V.weight, theta = V.mult, M = V.carrier, closed balls B_s, open ball B°_rho, omega_n = unitBallVolume n.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∃ C δP : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ 0 < δP ∧ δP ≤ 1 / 8 ∧ C * δP ≤ 1 / 2 ∧ ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ : ℝ), 0 < δ → δ ≤ δP → V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → (∀ y : Amb n ℓ, ‖y‖ ≤ 3 * δ * ρ → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ ρ / 2 → V.weight (closedBall y s) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + C * δ) * (unitBallVolume n * s ^ n))) ∧ (∀ y ∈ V.support, ‖y‖ ≤ 3 * δ * ρ → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s ≤ ρ / 2 → ENNReal.ofReal ((1 - C * δ) * (unitBallVolume n * s ^ n)) ≤ V.weight (closedBall y s)) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ‖x‖ ≤ 3 * δ * ρ → V.mult x ≤ 1 + C * δ) ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Amb n ℓ)) ((V.support ∩ ball 0 ρ) \ V.carrier) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 5, 2.4 ("by the monotonicity formula 4.7 and the semi-continuity 4.9 of Ch. 4 ..."), with explicit constants; Ch. 4, 4.10(1); Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2); Ch. 1, 3.6 (Upper Density Theorem). Corrections to the printed text:
- Lambda = delta/kappa with kappa = (p-n)/(4p).
- The bounds are proved only for delta <= delta_P(n,p) and centres |y| <= 3 delta rho.
- The monotonicity is applied on (0, (1 - 4 delta) rho] inside the ball B_{(1-3 delta) rho}(y), which is contained in B_rho(0).
No Chapter04 library structure is used: the monotonicity input is the child ted_lp_monotonicity, proved directly for the contract varifold.

Notation. mu := V.weight; theta := V.mult; M := V.carrier; spt V := V.support = U cap spt mu. B_s(y) := closedBall y s is the closed ball and B°_s(y) := ball y s the open ball. omega_n := unitBallVolume n > 0, H^n := μHE[n], and K(z,s) := V.scaledLpNorm H p z s. kappa := (p - n)/(4p) > 0 and alpha := 1 - n/p in (0,1).
(K-mono) If 0 < s <= t and B_s(z) ⊆ B_t(w), then K(z,s) <= K(w,t). Indeed s^{p-n} <= t^{p-n}, the lower integral is monotone in the set, and a |-> a^{1/p} is monotone.
(A) AllardHypotheses H p delta rho states: rho > 0; V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H; theta >= 1 mu-a.e.; 0 in spt V; B_rho(0) ⊆ U; mu(B_rho(0)) <= ofReal((1+delta) omega_n rho^n); and K(0,rho) <= ofReal(delta). Since ofReal(rho^{p-n}) > 0, integral^-_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p dmu < infinity. By (K-mono), K(z,s) <= ofReal(delta) whenever 0 < s <= rho and B_s(z) ⊆ B_rho(0). Finally mu(K) < infinity for compact K ⊆ U (V.integrableOn_mult).

Inputs.
(LM) ted_lp_monotonicity.
(D1) ted_density_ge_one.
(T3) ted_tangent_plane_facts, conclusion (3): for mu-a.e. x, V.HasDensity x (theta x).
(UD) Upper Density Theorem [Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6, stated for any metric space, here R^{n+l}]. Let lambda be a Borel regular outer measure and A a lambda-measurable set with lambda(A) < infinity. Then the set of x not in A with limsup_{r -> 0+} lambda(A cap B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) != 0 is null for Simon's n-dimensional Hausdorff measure (SimonGMT simonHausdorffMeasureReal n = (omega_n/2^n) μH[n], a positive finite multiple of μH[n]). Three facts make it applicable here:
- the outer measure of mu is Borel regular (SimonGMT Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular);
- Borel sets are measurable for it;
- H^n = μHE[n] is a nonnegative multiple of μH[n] (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def).
Hence the exceptional set is also H^n-null.

1. Constants. Put
- A_n := 1 + n 2^{n+4};
- C_+ := A_n + (9 e^2 2^n/4 + 2e/omega_n)/kappa;
- C_- := (1 + 1/omega_n)/kappa;
- C := max{1, C_+, C_-};
- delta_P := min{1/8, kappa, 1/(2C)}.
Then C >= 1, 0 < delta_P <= 1/8 and C delta_P <= 1/2, and C, delta_P depend only on n and p.

2. Elementary inequalities. Let t in (0, min{1/8, kappa}], Lambda_t := t/kappa in (0,1], and a(t) := (1 + t)(1 - 4t)^{-n}; note 1 - 4t >= 1/2.
(E1) For x in [0,1]: e^x <= 1 + e x and e^{2x} <= 1 + 2 e^2 x (mean value theorem), and e^{-x} >= 1 - x.
(E2) For u in [0, 1/2]: (1 - u)^{-n} - 1 <= n u (1 - u)^{-n-1} <= n 2^{n+1} u. This is the mean value theorem; the derivative n(1 - v)^{-n-1} is increasing. With u = 4t, (1 - 4t)^{-n} <= 1 + n 2^{n+3} t, so a(t) <= (1 + t)(1 + n 2^{n+3} t) <= 1 + (1 + (9/8) n 2^{n+3}) t <= 1 + A_n t, using t <= 1/8. Also a(t) <= (9/8) 2^n.
(E3) Put g_+(t) := e^{2 Lambda_t} a(t) + 2 e^{Lambda_t} Lambda_t/omega_n. Then
 g_+(t) <= (1 + 2 e^2 Lambda_t) a(t) + 2 e Lambda_t/omega_n <= 1 + A_n t + (9 e^2 2^n/4) Lambda_t + 2 e Lambda_t/omega_n = 1 + C_+ t <= 1 + C t.
(E4) Put g_-(t) := e^{-Lambda_t}(1 - Lambda_t/omega_n). Then g_-(t) >= 1 - Lambda_t - Lambda_t/omega_n = 1 - C_- t >= 1 - C t. To see this, let c := 1 - Lambda_t/omega_n <= 1. If c >= 0, then e^{-Lambda_t} c >= (1 - Lambda_t) c >= c - Lambda_t. If c < 0, then e^{-Lambda_t} c >= c >= c - Lambda_t.

3. Setting and monotonicity. Let U be open, and let V, H, 0 < delta <= delta_P and rho satisfy AllardHypotheses H p delta rho, unpacked in (A). Then delta <= 1/8 and delta <= kappa, and Lambda := delta/kappa in (0,1] satisfies kappa Lambda = delta.
Fix y with |y| <= 3 delta rho, and put S_y := (1 - 3 delta) rho and R_y := (1 - 4 delta) rho. Then rho/2 <= R_y < S_y, and B_{S_y}(y) ⊆ B_rho(0) ⊆ U because |x| <= |y| + S_y <= rho. By (A), integral^-_{B_{S_y}(y)} |H|^p dmu <= integral^-_{B_rho(0)} |H|^p dmu < infinity and K(y, R_y) <= ofReal(delta) = ofReal(kappa Lambda).
So (LM) applies at (y, R_y, S_y, Lambda). It gives F_y with e^{-Lambda} <= F_y(t) <= e^Lambda and |F_y(t) - 1| <= Lambda (t/R_y)^alpha <= Lambda for t in (0, R_y] (Lambda <= 1). It also gives that Phi_y(t) := F_y(t) t^{-n} mu(B_t(y)) + F_y(t) - 1 is nondecreasing on (0, R_y].
Since mu(B_{R_y}(y)) <= mu(B_rho(0)) <= (1 + delta) omega_n rho^n, we get R_y^{-n} mu(B_{R_y}(y)) <= (1 + delta)(1 - 4 delta)^{-n} omega_n = a(delta) omega_n. Hence
 Phi_y(R_y) <= e^Lambda a(delta) omega_n + Lambda. (3.1)

4. First conclusion (upper mass bound). Let |y| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < s <= rho/2, so s <= R_y. Then
 F_y(s) s^{-n} mu(B_s(y)) = Phi_y(s) - (F_y(s) - 1) <= Phi_y(R_y) + Lambda <= e^Lambda a(delta) omega_n + 2 Lambda.
Dividing by F_y(s) >= e^{-Lambda} gives
 s^{-n} mu(B_s(y)) <= e^{2 Lambda} a(delta) omega_n + 2 e^Lambda Lambda = omega_n g_+(delta) <= (1 + C delta) omega_n,
by (E3) with t = delta. As mu(B_s(y)) < infinity, mu(B_s(y)) <= ofReal((1 + C delta)(omega_n s^n)).

5. Second conclusion (lower mass bound). Let y in spt V with |y| <= 3 delta rho and 0 < s <= rho/2. Since |y| <= 3 rho/8 < rho, y in spt V cap B°_rho(0).
(a) Phi_y(t) >= omega_n for every t in (0, R_y]. Given eps in (0,1), (D1) gives u_0 > 0 with mu(B_u(y)) >= (1 - eps) omega_n u^n for all u in (0, u_0). For u in (0, min{u_0, t}), monotonicity and F_y(u) >= 1 - Lambda (u/R_y)^alpha give
 Phi_y(t) >= Phi_y(u) >= F_y(u)(1 - eps) omega_n + F_y(u) - 1 >= (1 - Lambda (u/R_y)^alpha)(1 - eps) omega_n - Lambda (u/R_y)^alpha.
Letting u -> 0+ gives Phi_y(t) >= (1 - eps) omega_n, and letting eps -> 0+ gives the claim.
(b) Hence F_y(s) s^{-n} mu(B_s(y)) = Phi_y(s) - (F_y(s) - 1) >= omega_n - Lambda. By (E4), g_-(delta) = e^{-Lambda}(1 - Lambda/omega_n) >= 1 - C delta >= 1/2, so omega_n - Lambda > 0. Since 0 < F_y(s) <= e^Lambda,
 s^{-n} mu(B_s(y)) >= e^{-Lambda}(omega_n - Lambda) = omega_n g_-(delta) >= (1 - C delta) omega_n.
Thus ofReal((1 - C delta)(omega_n s^n)) <= mu(B_s(y)).

6. Third conclusion (multiplicity). By (T3) there is a mu-null set N_1 such that, for x outside N_1, mu(B_r(x))/ofReal(omega_n r^n) -> ofReal(theta(x)) as r -> 0+. Let x be outside N_1 with |x| <= 3 delta rho. By Step 4, for r in (0, rho/2], mu(B_r(x)) <= ofReal(1 + C delta) ofReal(omega_n r^n), so the quotient is <= ofReal(1 + C delta). Passing to the limit, ofReal(theta(x)) <= ofReal(1 + C delta), hence theta(x) <= 1 + C delta, since 1 + C delta > 0. So theta(x) <= 1 + C delta for mu-a.e. x with |x| <= 3 delta rho.

7. Fourth conclusion (carrier).
(a) M is H^n-null-measurable (a contract field), so there is a Borel set B ⊆ M with H^n(M \ B) = 0 (Mathlib NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq). Then mu(R^{n+l} \ B) = integral_{(R^{n+l} \ B) cap M} ofReal(theta) dH^n = 0, because H^n((R^{n+l} \ B) cap M) = H^n(M \ B) = 0.
(b) Let A := B cap B_rho(0). A is Borel, and mu(A) <= mu(B_rho(0)) < infinity since B_rho(0) is a compact subset of U. By (UD), the set E_0 := {x not in A : limsup_{r -> 0+} mu(A cap B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) != 0} satisfies H^n(E_0) = 0.
(c) Let x in (spt V cap B°_rho(0)) \ M. Then x is not in A, because A ⊆ M. For 0 < r < rho - |x|, B_r(x) ⊆ B_rho(0), so A cap B_r(x) = B cap B_r(x), and mu(A cap B_r(x)) = mu(B_r(x)) by (a). By (D1) with eps = 1/2 (x in spt V cap B°_rho(0)), mu(B_r(x)) >= (1/2) omega_n r^n for all sufficiently small r > 0. So the limsup is >= 1/2 and x in E_0.
Hence (spt V cap B°_rho(0)) \ M ⊆ E_0, and H^n((V.support cap ball 0 rho) \ V.carrier) = 0.

8. Steps 1 and 4-7 give the four conclusions. The constants C >= 1 and delta_P satisfy 0 < delta_P <= 1/8 and C delta_P <= 1/2, and depend only on n and p (hence only on n, l, p).
proof_key_steps: Explicit constants C, delta_P from the elementary bounds g_+(t) <= 1 + C t and g_-(t) >= 1 - C t on (0, min(1/8, kappa)]
ted_lp_monotonicity at |y| <= 3 delta rho with R = (1-4 delta)rho, S = (1-3 delta)rho, Lambda = delta/kappa <= 1
Upper mass bound from Phi(s) <= Phi(R) and mu(B_R(y)) <= mu(B_rho(0)) <= (1+delta) omega_n rho^n
Lower mass bound: ted_density_ge_one gives Phi >= omega_n on (0,R], hence s^-n mu(B_s(y)) >= omega_n g_-(delta)
theta <= 1 + C delta mu-a.e. on {|x| <= 3 delta rho} from HasDensity a.e. (ted_tangent_plane_facts (3)) and the upper bound

subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation. For f : R^n -> R^l, f^j(x) := (f x) j is the j-th coordinate, grad f^j(x) := gradient (fun y => f y j) x (the pointwise gradient, 0 where f^j is not differentiable), Df(x) := fderiv f x and |Df(x)|^2 := hsNormSq (Df(x)) = sum_j |grad f^j(x)|^2 at points where f is differentiable. B_s := B_s(0) closed and B°_s := ball 0 s open in R^n; the sphere is L^n-null, so integrals over B_s and B°_s agree. omega_n := unitBallVolume n = L^n(B_1).

Cited facts.
(Lip) If g : R^n -> R is Lipschitz on the closed ball B_1, then IsW12WithGradient g (grad g) (ball 0 1). Indeed g is bounded and continuous on B_1; by Rademacher (Simon Ch. 2, 1.4; Mathlib Rademacher) g is differentiable a.e. on B°_1 with |grad g| <= Lip g there, so grad g is bounded and Borel (Mathlib measurable_fderiv), hence both are in L^2(B°_1); and for zeta in C^infinity_c(R^n) with tsupport zeta contained in B°_1, int_{B°_1} g grad zeta = - int_{B°_1} zeta grad g: extend g from B_1 to a Lipschitz function g~ on R^n (McShane, Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real), which changes nothing on tsupport zeta; then Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq (integration by parts along lines, with lineDeriv = grad g~ . e_i a.e.) gives the identity coordinatewise; on B°_1 the a.e. gradients of g and g~ agree.
(Harm) [Simon 3.2-3.4, from the mean value property of harmonic functions] There is C_H = C_H(n) >= 1 such that if v : R^n -> R is harmonic on B°_1 (InnerProductSpace.HarmonicOnNhd v (ball 0 1)) and v, grad v are in L^2(B°_1), then |v(0)| <= C_H ||v||_{L^2(B_1)}, |grad v(0)| <= C_H ||grad v||_{L^2(B_1)}, and sup_{z in B_e} |v(z) - v(0) - grad v(0) . z| <= C_H e^2 ||grad v||_{L^2(B_1)} for every e in (0, 1/4]. (By the mean value property on balls of radius 1/4 centred in B_{1/2}, sup_{B_{1/2}} |v| <= C ||v||_{L^1(B_1)} and sup_{B_{1/2}} |D^k v| <= C(k, n) ||grad v||_{L^1(B_1)} for k >= 1, applied to the harmonic functions D_i v; Taylor's formula of order 2 at 0 on B_e, contained in B_{1/4}, gives |v(z) - v(0) - grad v(0) . z| <= (1/2) e^2 sup_{B_{1/4}} |D^2 v|; Cauchy-Schwarz converts L^1 into L^2 norms on B_1.)

Proof.
1. Constants. Put C := max{ sqrt(l) C_H (1 + omega_n^{1/2}), 2 l (1 + omega_n C_H^2), 1 }; C depends only on n and l. Given eps in (0, 1), let delta_eps > 0 be the delta that HarmonicApproximationLemma (the hypothesis) provides for n and eps.

2. Rescaled components. Let r, E, h, f, L satisfy the hypotheses (with delta_eps), and fix j. Define F_j(z) := f^j(r z)/(r sqrt(E)), z in R^n. F_j is Lipschitz on B_1 (f is Lipschitz on B_r), so by (Lip), IsW12WithGradient F_j G_j (ball 0 1) with G_j := gradient F_j. For every z, G_j(z) = E^{-1/2} grad f^j(r z): if f^j is differentiable at r z this is the chain rule; otherwise F_j is not differentiable at z (because f^j(x) = r sqrt(E) F_j(x/r)) and both sides are 0.

3. Energy. f is differentiable at a.e. x in B°_r (Rademacher), and there |grad f^j(x)|^2 <= sum_i |grad f^i(x)|^2 = |Df(x)|^2. Changing variables x = r z,
 int_{B°_1} |G_j|^2 dz = E^{-1} r^{-n} int_{B°_r} |grad f^j|^2 dx <= E^{-1} r^{-n} int_{B°_r} |Df|^2 dx <= E^{-1} r^{-n} E r^n = 1,
so the extended integral int^-_{ball 0 1} ||G_j||_e^2 is at most 1.

4. Almost harmonicity. Let zeta in C^infinity(R^n) have compact support with tsupport zeta contained in B°_1, and let M satisfy |grad zeta| <= M everywhere. Put zeta_0(x) := zeta(x/r). Then zeta_0 is C^infinity with compact support, tsupport zeta_0 = r tsupport zeta is contained in B°_r, and grad zeta_0(x) = r^{-1} grad zeta(x/r), so |grad zeta_0| <= M/r. By the change of variables x = r z,
 int_{B°_1} G_j . grad zeta dz = E^{-1/2} int_{B°_1} grad f^j(r z) . r grad zeta_0(r z) dz = E^{-1/2} r^{1-n} int_{B°_r} grad f^j . grad zeta_0 dx.
The hypothesis applied to zeta_0 with the bound M/r gives |int_{B°_r} grad f^j . grad zeta_0| <= delta_eps sqrt(E) (M/r) r^n, hence |int_{B°_1} G_j . grad zeta| <= delta_eps M. So (F_j, G_j) satisfies all hypotheses of HarmonicApproximationLemma with delta = delta_eps.

5. Harmonic approximants. HarmonicApproximationLemma yields U_j : R^n -> R, harmonic on B°_1, with int^-_{B°_1} |grad U_j|^2 <= 1 and int^-_{B°_1} |U_j - F_j|^2 <= eps. Since |f| <= h on B°_r, |F_j| <= h/(r sqrt(E)) on B°_1, so ||F_j||_{L^2(B_1)} <= omega_n^{1/2} h/(r sqrt(E)) and ||U_j||_{L^2(B_1)} <= ||U_j - F_j|| + ||F_j|| <= sqrt(eps) + omega_n^{1/2} h/(r sqrt(E)) < infinity; also ||grad U_j||_{L^2(B_1)} <= 1. So (Harm) applies to v = U_j.

6. Definition of a and A. a := (r sqrt(E) U_j(0))_{j=1..l} in R^l and A x := (sqrt(E) grad U_j(0) . x)_{j=1..l}, a linear map R^n -> R^l.
 (i) hsNormSq A = sum_i |A e_i|^2 = E sum_j |grad U_j(0)|^2 <= E l C_H^2, so hsNorm A <= sqrt(l) C_H sqrt(E) <= C sqrt(E).
 (ii) |a_j| = r sqrt(E) |U_j(0)| <= r sqrt(E) C_H (sqrt(eps) + omega_n^{1/2} h/(r sqrt(E))) = C_H (r sqrt(eps E) + omega_n^{1/2} h), so ||a|| <= sqrt(l) C_H (1 + omega_n^{1/2})(h + r sqrt(eps E)) <= C (h + r sqrt(eps E)).
 (iii) Let e in (0, 1/4] and Lambda_j(z) := U_j(0) + grad U_j(0) . z. For x = r z, f^j(x) - a_j - (A x)_j = r sqrt(E)(F_j(z) - Lambda_j(z)), so
 int_{B°_{e r}} |f(x) - (a + A x)|^2 dx = r^{n+2} E sum_j int_{B°_e} |F_j - Lambda_j|^2 dz.
By (Harm) with ||grad U_j||_{L^2(B_1)} <= 1, |U_j - Lambda_j| <= C_H e^2 on B_e, hence
 int_{B°_e} |F_j - Lambda_j|^2 <= 2 int_{B°_e} |F_j - U_j|^2 + 2 int_{B°_e} |U_j - Lambda_j|^2 <= 2 eps + 2 omega_n e^n C_H^2 e^4.
Summing over j: int_{B°_{e r}} |f - (a + A x)|^2 dx <= 2 l (eps + omega_n C_H^2 e^{n+4}) E r^{n+2} <= C (eps + e^{n+4}) E r^{n+2}.

7. (i)-(iii) are the three conclusions; C does not depend on eps, r, E, h, f, L, and delta_eps depends only on n and eps. (If l = 0 everything is trivial with a = 0, A = 0.)

Apply 3.1 to obtain harmonic U_j that are L^2-close to F_j
Mean-value estimates (Simon 3.2-3.4) at the origin
Define a, A from U_j(0), grad U_j(0) and bound them
Estimate f - (a + A x) in L^2(B_{e r}) by splitting through U_j

F(x') := q(graphPoint(x', f(x'))), Gamma := F(B^n_{sigma/2}) = q '' graphOver f (closedBall 0 (sigma/2)), M_1 := M_V cap Gamma. f^j(x') := (f x') j, grad f^j := gradient (fun y => f y j), Df := fderiv f, |Df|^2 := hsNormSq (Df). (Rad) [Simon Ch. 2, 1.4; Mathlib Rademacher] f is differentiable at L^n-a.e. x' in B°^n_{sigma/2}; there ||Df(x')|| <= 1 (f is 1-Lipschitz on B^n_{sigma/2}), hence |grad f^j(x')| <= 1 for every j, |Df(x')|^2 = sum_j |grad f^j(x')|^2 <= n, and at such points the gradient of the j-th coordinate is the j-th row of Df. (Area) [Simon Ch. 2, Sect. 3; SimonGMT Chapter02.injective_area_formula_lipschitz_simon] F is injective and Lipschitz (|F(x') - F(y')|^2 = |x' - y'|^2 + |f(x') - f(y')|^2 <= 2|x' - y'|^2), and for Borel A contained in B°^n_{sigma/2} and Borel phi >= 0, int_{F(A)} phi dH^n = int_A phi(F(x')) J_F(x') dx' with J_F = det(I + Df^T Df)^{1/2}. Since a o F = id and a is 1-Lipschitz, L^n(A) <= H^n(F(A)) <= 2^{n/2} L^n(A); so F maps L^n-null sets to H^n-null sets and preimages under F of H^n-null subsets of Gamma are L^n-null. (Jac) For an l x n matrix D with ||D|| <= 1 and singular values s_i in [0, 1]: |D|^2 = sum s_i^2 <= n, J(D) := det(I + D^T D)^{1/2} = prod (1 + s_i^2)^{1/2} is in [1, 2^{n/2}], and J(D) <= exp(|D|^2/2) <= 1 + c_n |D|^2 (as e^t <= 1 + t e^t for t >= 0 and |D|^2/2 <= n/2). Proof. Let C_7 := l + 1/2 + n K_b and C := max{C_7, 2 K_b + 1 + c_n C_7, (1 + c_n n)(omega_n C_7)^{1/2}, 1}; C depends only on n, l, K_b.

1. Localization. (a) If x in spt V cap B_sigma(0) and |a(x)| < sigma/4, then |x| <= |a(x)| + |b(x)| < sigma/4 + sigma/16 = 5 sigma/16 by the height hypothesis. and the integrand on the left vanishes for mu-a.e. x outside B_{5 sigma/16}(0). All integrands are mu-measurable (x |-> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable by hypothesis), bounded apart from H (integrable on B_sigma(0)), and supported in B_{sigma/2}(0), of finite measure.

P (I - p_x) P w, and P (I - p_x) P = (P - p_x)(I - p_x)(P - p_x) (expand, using p_x (I - p_x) = 0 and (I - p_x)(P - p_x) = (I - p_x) P). Hence |(p_x u) . (p_x w) - u . w| <= ||P - p_x||^2 |u| |w| <= |p_x - P|^2 |u| |w|. With u = g_j(x), w = grad zeta~(x) (|g_j| <= 1, |grad zeta~| <= M), and int_{B_sigma(0)} |p_x - P|^2 dmu <= E sigma^n:
 (12) |int_{M_1 cap B_{sigma/2}(0)} g_j . grad zeta~ dmu| <= (K_b E + h/4) M sigma^n + M E sigma^n.
With u = w = g_j: |g_j|^2 <= |p_x g_j|^2 + |p_x - P|^2 = |p_x e'_j|^2 + |p_x - P|^2 mu-a.e. on M_1 (step 3). Where p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace (mu-a.e. on M_1 by step 3), sum_j |p_x e'_j|^2 = sum_j e'_j . p_x e'_j = trace(Q p_x Q) = trace(p_x) - trace(P p_x) = (1/2)|p_x - P|^2 (as |p_x - P|^2 = trace((p_x - P)^2) = 2n - 2 trace(P p_x)). Therefore
 (13) int_{M_1 cap B_{sigma/2}(0)} sum_j |g_j|^2 dmu <= (l + 1/2) int_{B_sigma(0)} |p_x - P|^2 dmu <= (l + 1/2) E sigma^n.

6. The set N (book (4c)). N := {x' in B°^n_{3 sigma/8} : F(x') not in M_V}. For x' in N, F(x') lies in B°_{sigma/2}(0) cap Gamma (1(b)) and not in M_V; either F(x') is not in spt V, so F(x') lies in B_{sigma/2}(0) cap (Gamma \ spt V), or F(x') lies in (spt V cap B_sigma(0)) \ M_V. By the bad-set hypothesis (second summand) and the carrier hypothesis, H^n(F(N)) <= K_b E sigma^n + 0, and so L^n(N) <= H^n(F(N)) <= K_b E sigma^n (N is L^n-measurable: F^{-1} of the H^n-null-measurable set M_V is L^n-measurable by (Area)).

7. Multiplicity and Jacobian along the graph. For a.e. x' in B°^n_{3 sigma/8} \ N (namely where f is differentiable and the multiplicity hypothesis holds at F(x'); the exceptional set is the preimage under F of an H^n-null subset of M_V cap B_sigma(0), hence L^n-null), 1 <= theta(F(x')) <= 1 + kappa and, by (Jac), 1 <= J_F(x') <= 1 + c_n |Df(x')|^2; so 1 <= theta(F) J_F and theta(F) J_F - 1 <= (1 + kappa)(1 + c_n |Df|^2) - 1 <= kappa (1 + c_n n) + c_n |Df|^2. Transfer formula: since mu = theta H^n restricted to M_V and F(A) cap M_V = F(A \ N), for Borel A contained in B°^n_{3 sigma/8} and Borel phi (nonnegative, or bounded),
 int_{M_1 cap F(A)} phi dmu = int_{A \ N} phi(F(x')) theta(F(x')) J_F(x') dx'.

8. Energy bound (book (16), first conclusion). At differentiability points |Df(x')|^2 = sum_j |g_j(F(x'))|^2. By steps 6, 7 (with A = B°^n_{3 sigma/8}, F(A) contained in B_{sigma/2}(0)) and (13):
 int_{B°^n_{3 sigma/8}} |Df|^2 dx' <= int_{B°^n_{3 sigma/8} \ N} sum_j |g_j(F)|^2 theta(F) J_F dx' + n L^n(N) = int_{M_1 cap F(A)} sum_j |g_j|^2 dmu + n L^n(N) <= (l + 1/2) E sigma^n + n K_b E sigma^n = C_7 E sigma^n <= C E sigma^n.

9. Weak equation (book (15), second conclusion). For x' in B°^n_{sigma/2} with f differentiable at x', g_j(F(x')) . grad zeta~(F(x')) = grad f^j(x') . grad zeta(x') (q is an isometry). The integrand g_j . grad zeta~ on M_1 cap B_{sigma/2}(0) vanishes outside F(B°^n_{sigma/4}) (if x = F(x') with |x'| >= sigma/4 then a(x) = x' is not in tsupport zeta). So by step 7 with A = B°^n_{sigma/4}:
 int_{M_1 cap B_{sigma/2}(0)} g_j . grad zeta~ dmu = int_{B°^n_{sigma/4} \ N} (grad f^j . grad zeta) theta(F) J_F dx',
and therefore
 int_{B°^n_{sigma/4}} grad f^j . grad zeta dx' - int_{M_1 cap B_{sigma/2}(0)} g_j . grad zeta~ dmu = int_{N cap B°^n_{sigma/4}} grad f^j . grad zeta dx' - int_{B°^n_{sigma/4} \ N} (grad f^j . grad zeta)(theta(F) J_F - 1) dx'.
The first term is at most M L^n(N) <= M K_b E sigma^n. By step 7, |grad f^j| <= min{1, |Df|}, Cauchy-Schwarz and step 8, the second is at most
 M int_{B°^n_{sigma/4}} |grad f^j| (kappa (1 + c_n n) + c_n |Df|^2) dx' <= M [kappa (1 + c_n n)(omega_n (sigma/4)^n)^{1/2}(C_7 E sigma^n)^{1/2} + c_n C_7 E sigma^n].
Together with (12):
 |int_{B°^n_{sigma/4}} grad f^j . grad zeta dx'| <= M sigma^n [(2 K_b + 1 + c_n C_7) E + h/4 + (1 + c_n n)(omega_n C_7)^{1/2} kappa sqrt(E)] <= C (E + h + kappa sqrt(E)) M sigma^n.
This is the second conclusion (the integral is over ball 0 (sigma/4), with integrand inner (gradient (fun y => f y j) x') (gradient zeta x')).
proof_key_steps: Localize with the height bounds and a cutoff h_c equal to 1 on B_{3 sigma/8}(0)
First-variation identity (6) with X = h_c (zeta o a) e'_j
On the graph p_x e'_j = p_x g_j by the tangent identification
Error terms off the graph (bad set) and from H
Remove p_x at cost |p_x - P|^2; sum_j |p_x e'_j|^2 = |p_x - P|^2/2
Graph points off the carrier form a set of measure <= K_b E sigma^n
Transfer to parameter space with 1 <= theta(F) J_F <= 1 + kappa(1 + c_n n) + c_n |Df|^2
Energy bound (16) and weak equation (15)

subproblems.title: Tilt bounded by L2 height and sup-height times L1 mean curvature (Lemma A)
subproblems.statement: Let n >= 1, l, U open, V with generalized mean curvature H in U, x |-> p_x mu-a.e. strongly measurable and mu-a.e. the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace. If z in R^{n+l}, r > 0 with B_r(z) in U, h >= 0, T is an n-dimensional subspace and infDist(x - z, T) <= h for every x in spt V cap B_r(z), then int_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 144 r^{-2} int_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + 4 h int_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ), V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H → AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight → (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ∃ P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ P = n ∧ V.tangentProj x = P.starProjection) → ∀ (z : Amb n ℓ) (r h : ℝ), 0 < r → closedBall z r ⊆ U → 0 ≤ h → ∀ T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ T = n → (∀ x ∈ V.support ∩ closedBall z r, infDist (x - z) (T : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ≤ h) → ∫ x in closedBall z (r / 2), hsNormSq (V.tangentProj x - T.starProjection) ∂V.weight ≤ 144 * (r ^ 2)⁻¹ * ∫ x in closedBall z r, infDist (x - z) (T : Set (Amb n ℓ)) ^ 2 ∂V.weight + 4 * h * ∫ x in closedBall z r, ‖H x‖ ∂V.weight
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation. mu := V.weight, p_x := V.tangentProj x, p_T := T.starProjection, |A|^2 := hsNormSq A (Hilbert-Schmidt), ||A|| operator norm (||A|| <= |A|), spt V := V.support. B_s(z) closed ball, B°_s(z) open ball. x' := p_{T^perp}(x - z), so |x'| = dist(x - z, T) = infDist (x - z) T.

Basic facts used. (F2) mu-a.e. point lies in spt V (mu(R^{n+l} \ spt mu) = 0 and mu(R^{n+l} \ U) = 0); mu(K) < infinity for compact K contained in U (contract integrableOn_mult); H is mu-integrable on compact subsets of U (first conjunct of HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature). The hypotheses give: x |-> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, and for mu-a.e. x, p_x = P.starProjection for an n-dimensional subspace P (a rank-n orthogonal projection).

Proof.
1. Cut-off. Fix phi in C^infinity(R, [0, 1]) with phi = 1 on (-infinity, 1/2], phi = 0 on [1, infinity) and |phi'| <= 3 (possible since the transition interval has length 1/2). Put zeta(x) := phi(|x - z|/r). zeta is C^infinity (phi is constant near 0, so the non-smoothness of |x - z| at z is irrelevant), 0 <= zeta <= 1, zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z), zeta = 0 outside B°_r(z), and |grad zeta| <= 3/r.

2. Test field. X(x) := zeta(x)^2 x'. X is C^infinity, has compact support, and tsupport X is contained in B_r(z), which is contained in U; so X is admissible in the definition of generalized mean curvature: int div_M X dmu = - int X . H dmu. X . H is mu-integrable because H is integrable on the compact set B_r(z) and X is bounded.

3. Divergence. DX(x) v = zeta^2 p_{T^perp} v + 2 zeta (grad zeta . v) x'. At every x where p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace (mu-a.e. x by hypothesis):
 div_M X(x) = trace(DX(x) o p_x) = zeta^2 trace(p_{T^perp} p_x) + 2 zeta grad zeta . p_x x' = zeta^2 s + 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x',
where s := (1/2)|p_x - p_T|^2. Here trace(v |-> (w . p_x v) u) = w . p_x u was used; p_T x' = 0; and for rank-n orthogonal projections trace(p_{T^perp} p_x) = trace(p_x) - trace(p_T p_x) = n - trace(p_T p_x) = (1/2)|p_x - p_T|^2, because |p_x - p_T|^2 = trace((p_x - p_T)^2) = trace(p_x) + trace(p_T) - 2 trace(p_T p_x) = 2n - 2 trace(p_T p_x).

4. Integrability. All integrands (zeta^2 s, zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x', zeta^2 |x'||H|, |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2) are mu-measurable (x |-> p_x is mu-measurable by hypothesis), bounded except for the factor |H|, which is integrable on B_r(z), and vanish outside B_r(z), which has finite mu-measure. So all integrals below are finite.

5. Identity. By steps 2 and 3, int zeta^2 s dmu = - int 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x' dmu - int zeta^2 x' . H dmu.

6. Absorption. |(p_x - p_T) x'| <= ||p_x - p_T|| |x'| <= |p_x - p_T| |x'| = sqrt(2s) |x'|. By 2AB <= t A^2 + B^2/t with t = 1/2, A = zeta sqrt(s), B = sqrt(2) |grad zeta| |x'|:
 |2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x'| <= 2 sqrt(2) zeta sqrt(s) |grad zeta| |x'| <= (1/2) zeta^2 s + 4 |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2.
Hence int zeta^2 s <= (1/2) int zeta^2 s + 4 int |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 + int zeta^2 |x'| |H|, and since int zeta^2 s is finite,
 int zeta^2 s dmu <= 8 int |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 dmu + 2 int zeta^2 |x'| |H| dmu.

7. Conclusion. zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z), 0 <= zeta <= 1, |grad zeta| <= 3/r, zeta = 0 off B_r(z), and |x'| <= h for mu-a.e. x in B_r(z) (such x lie in spt V by (F2), and the hypothesis gives infDist (x - z) T <= h there). Therefore
 (1/2) int_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= int zeta^2 s dmu <= 72 r^{-2} int_{B_r(z)} |x'|^2 dmu + 2 h int_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu,
and multiplying by 2:
 int_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 144 r^{-2} int_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + 4 h int_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu,
which is the claim (the left side is the Bochner integral of the integrable function hsNormSq (V.tangentProj x - T.starProjection) over closedBall z (r/2)).
proof_key_steps: Cut-off zeta and test field X = zeta^2 p_{T^perp}(x - z)
div_M X = zeta^2 |p_x - p_T|^2/2 + 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x' mu-a.e.
First-variation identity; integrability
Absorb the cross term by Young's inequality
Use zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z), |grad zeta| <= 3/r and |x'| <= h

subproblems.title: Tilt-excess decay at the origin at the natural scale delta rho
subproblems.statement: Assume the contract Props TiltExcessHeightEstimate (Simon 2.1), AffineApproximationLemma (2.5), LipschitzApproximationLemma (2.6) and HarmonicApproximationLemma (3.1). For n >= 1, l and p > n there is C > 0 such that for every t in (0, 1/128] there is delta_1 > 0 with the property: if U is open, V has generalized mean curvature H and AllardHypotheses H p delta rho hold with 0 < delta <= delta_1, then for every n-dimensional subspace T there is an n-dimensional subspace S with E(0, t delta rho, S) <= C t^2 E_*(0, delta rho, T), where E = tiltExcess and E_* = tiltExcessStar with this delta.
subproblems.lean_statement: TiltExcessHeightEstimate → AffineApproximationLemma → LipschitzApproximationLemma → HarmonicApproximationLemma → ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ, (n : ℝ) < p → ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → t ≤ 1 / 128 → ∃ δ₁ : ℝ, 0 < δ₁ ∧ ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U) (H : Amb n ℓ → Amb n ℓ) (δ ρ : ℝ), 0 < δ → δ ≤ δ₁ → V.AllardHypotheses H p δ ρ → ∀ T : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ T = n → ∃ S : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ S = n ∧ V.tiltExcess 0 (t * (δ * ρ)) S ≤ C * t ^ 2 * V.tiltExcessStar H p δ 0 (δ * ρ) T
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation. alpha := 1 - n/p in (0, 1); gamma := 1/(2n+2) (so 2 gamma = 1/(n+1) <= 1/2; gamma is the exponent written 1/(2*n+2) in the contract). For the varifold V: mu := V.weight, M_V := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, spt V := V.support, p_x := V.tangentProj x, p_S := S.starProjection, |A|^2 := hsNormSq A, ||A|| the operator norm (||A|| <= |A|). B_s(z) closed ball, B°_s(z) open ball; omega_n := unitBallVolume n; c_omega := max{1, 2 omega_n}. K(z, s) := (V.scaledLpNorm H p z s).toReal; E(z, s, S) := V.tiltExcess z s S; E_*(z, s, S) := V.tiltExcessStar H p delta z s S = max{E(z, s, S), delta^{-1} K(z, s)^2}. For a linear map A : R^n -> R^l, graph A := span{graphPoint(v, A v) : v in R^n}. The letter M is reserved for gradient bounds of test functions.

Inputs. The four hypotheses 2.1 (TiltExcessHeightEstimate), 2.5 (AffineApproximationLemma), 2.6 (LipschitzApproximationLemma), 3.1 (HarmonicApproximationLemma), and the sibling theorems:
(B) ted_allard_density_bounds: constants C_P >= 1, 0 < delta_P <= 1/8, C_P delta_P <= 1/2 such that AllardHypotheses H p delta rho with 0 < delta <= delta_P imply: (B.i) mu(B_s(y)) <= (1 + C_P delta) omega_n s^n for |y| <= 3 delta rho, 0 < s <= rho/2; (B.ii) mu(B_s(y)) >= (1 - C_P delta) omega_n s^n >= omega_n s^n/2 if moreover y in spt V; (B.iii) theta <= 1 + C_P delta mu-a.e. on {|x| <= 3 delta rho}; (B.iv) H^n((spt V cap B°_rho(0)) \ M_V) = 0.
(C) ted_tangent_plane_facts, conclusions (1) mu-a.e. p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace; (2) x |-> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; (4) the identification of p_x on Lipschitz graphs.
(G) ted_harmonic_affine_approx (applied to the hypothesis 3.1): a constant C_G and, for each eps in (0,1), delta^G_eps > 0.
(I) ted_graph_weak_equation: for K_b := C_6 (below) a constant C_W > 0.
(J) ted_lemma_a_tilt_height.
Basic facts (F2): mu-a.e. point lies in spt V and in M_V; mu(K) < infinity for compact K contained in U; H is mu-integrable on compact subsets of U. By (C.2) and boundedness (|p_x - p_S|^2 <= 4n), x |-> |p_x - p_S|^2 is mu-integrable on every compact subset of U, so its integrals over nested balls are monotone. K-scaling: if B_s(z) is contained in B_t(w), which is contained in B_rho(0), then K(z, s) <= (s/t)^alpha K(w, t) <= K(w, t) and K(z, s) <= delta (monotonicity of the lower integral; K(0, rho) <= delta by 2.3; all values finite). (Area) and (Rad) as in Simon Ch. 2: area formula for injective Lipschitz graph maps; Rademacher. (Jac): for an l x n matrix A with ||A|| <= 1, J(A) := det(I + A^T A)^{1/2} <= 2^{n/2}, and ||p_{graph A} - p_{graph 0}|| <= 4 ||A|| (from p_{graph A} = [[G, G A^T], [A G, A G A^T]], G := (I + A^T A)^{-1}: ||G - I|| <= ||A||^2, ||G A^T|| = ||A G|| <= ||A||, ||A G A^T|| <= ||A||^2).

Constants (depending only on n, l, p). From 2.1: C_21; from 2.5: C_A; from 2.6: beta_6, C_6. We may and do assume C_21, C_A, C_6 >= 1 (enlarging them preserves the conclusions: in 2.1 and 2.6 the constant multiplies a nonnegative quantity inside ofReal; in 2.5 a larger C decreases C^{-1} on the left of the first inequality and increases the right side of the second). Put
 C_2 := 2^n C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2, C_3 := 2 C_A + 2 (8 C_2/omega_n)^{1/2}, C_4 := C_2 + 1, C_8 := C_4^{1/2} + c_omega + C_P,
 C_9 := 4^n C_W, C_10 := C_W C_8 4^n C_9^{-1/2}, C_11 := C_G (C_3 + (C_9 C_4)^{1/2}/4), C_12 := C_G C_9^{1/2}, C_13 := C_G C_9,
 C_14 := C_3 + 4 C_12 C_4^{1/2} + C_11, C_15 := max{2^{n/2+1} C_13, 4^{n+2} C_14^2 C_6}, C_17 := (8 C_G C_9)^{1/2} + ((2 C_W + C_12^2/4)/8)^{1/2}, C_18 := 2 C_17 + 2 C_6,
 C_19 := max{C_21 C_15, C_21 c_omega, 288 C_15, 128 C_18}, and finally C := 3 * 2^{n+8} C_19 > 0.

Proof.
0. Choice of delta_1. Let t in (0, 1/128]. Put eta := 16 t in (0, 1/8], eps := eta^{n+4} in (0, 1) and delta_eps := delta^G_eps. Choose delta_1 in (0, delta_P] so small that every delta in (0, delta_1] satisfies:
 (c1) delta <= 1/4 and delta <= beta_6^{2n+2}; (c2) C_4 delta^{2 gamma} <= 1; (c3) C_3 delta^gamma <= 1/16; (c4) C_10 delta^gamma <= delta_eps; (c5) C_11 delta^gamma <= eta/16; (c6) 4 C_12 C_4^{1/2} delta^gamma <= 1; (c7) C_14 delta^gamma <= 1/32; (c8) eta^{-n-2} delta^{2 gamma} + delta + eta^{-1} delta^{1/2} <= eta^2.
All left sides are constants times positive powers of delta, so such delta_1 > 0 exists (depending on n, l, p, t).

1. Setting. Let U be open, V, H, delta in (0, delta_1], rho with AllardHypotheses H p delta rho, and T with dim T = n. Put sigma := delta rho (so 2 sigma <= rho/2 and B_{2 sigma}(0) is contained in B°_rho(0)). By (B), for |y| <= 3 sigma and 0 < s <= rho/2: mu(B_s(y)) <= 2 omega_n s^n, and mu(B_s(y)) >= omega_n s^n/2 if y in spt V.

2. Reduction (book (1), (2)). Apply 2.5 with xi := 0 (in spt V cap B_{delta rho}(0)) and radius 2 sigma in (0, 2 delta rho]: there is an n-dimensional T~ with C_A^{-1}((2 sigma)^{-n} int_{B_sigma(0)} |p_x - p_T~|^2 dmu)^{1/2} <= (2 sigma)^{-1} heightSup(0, 2 sigma, T~) + K(0, 2 sigma) and (2 sigma)^{-1} heightSup(0, 2 sigma, T~) <= C_A delta^gamma. As K(0, 2 sigma) <= delta <= delta^gamma, E(0, sigma, T~) <= 2^n C_A^2 (C_A + 1)^2 delta^{2 gamma} = C_2 delta^{2 gamma}, and dist(x, T~) <= 2 C_A delta^gamma sigma for x in spt V cap B_{2 sigma}(0). If E(0, sigma, T) > C_2 delta^{2 gamma}, then E_*(0, sigma, T~) <= E_*(0, sigma, T) (the H-terms coincide), and any S with E(0, t sigma, S) <= C t^2 E_*(0, sigma, T~) also satisfies the claim for T; so we may assume (1) E(0, sigma, T) <= C_2 delta^{2 gamma}. Then |p_T - p_T~|^2 <= 2|p_x - p_T|^2 + 2|p_x - p_T~|^2 for every x; integrating over B_sigma(0), whose measure is >= omega_n sigma^n/2 (step 1, y = 0), gives (omega_n sigma^n/2)|p_T - p_T~|^2 <= 4 C_2 delta^{2 gamma} sigma^n, so ||p_T - p_T~|| <= (8 C_2/omega_n)^{1/2} delta^gamma. For x in spt V cap B_{2 sigma}(0): dist(x, T) = |x - p_T x| <= |x - p_T~ x| + ||p_T~ - p_T|| |x| <= C_3 delta^gamma sigma. (2)
Let E_0 := E_*(0, sigma, T). Since K(0, sigma) <= delta, delta^{-1} K(0, sigma)^2 <= delta <= delta^{2 gamma}; so E_0 <= C_4 delta^{2 gamma} <= 1 by (c2), and K(0, sigma)^2 <= delta E_0. (2')
If E_0 = 0, then int_{B_sigma(0)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu = 0, hence int_{B_{t sigma}(0)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu = 0, and S := T works. Assume E_0 > 0. Choose a linear isometry q of R^{n+l} with rotatedPlane q = T (send the standard basis, whose first n vectors span R^n x {0}, to an orthonormal basis of R^{n+l} whose first n vectors span T). Put P := p_T, and write q^{-1} x = graphPoint(a(x), b(x)) (a, b linear, |a(x)| <= |x|).

3. Lipschitz approximation (book (3), (4)). Apply 2.6 with L := 1, K := C_3, this q (heights by (2), delta <= beta_6^{2n+2} by (c1)): there is f : R^n -> R^l, 1-Lipschitz on B^n_{sigma/2}(0), with |f| <= C_3 delta^gamma sigma <= sigma/16 on B^n_{sigma/2}(0) (c3) and, for Gamma := q '' graphOver f (closedBall 0 (sigma/2)),
 (4) mu(B_{sigma/2}(0) cap (spt V \ Gamma)) + H^n(B_{sigma/2}(0) cap (Gamma \ spt V)) <= ofReal(C_6 int_{B_sigma(0)} |p_x - P|^2 dmu) <= ofReal(C_6 E_0 sigma^n).
